A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable, and relocated material can be reliably matched.

before.justification: v2 reports original stratified analyses of SummEval, SNLI/MNLI and MT-Bench, synthetic-label simulations, and appendix case-study results.

after.justification: v3 retains these original analyses and adds ordinal Topical Chat analyses in Appendix A.12.2, Table 11 and Figures 8–11.

M1.justification: The uncertainty-stratification procedure, median/majority binning, binned-JSD computation and perception-chart construction are retained. The added ordinal case study applies these existing procedures.

E1.justification: v3 extends Topical Chat evaluation with four ordinal criteria: Engaging, Maintains Context, Naturalness and Overall (A.12.2). The categorical Topical Chat, QAGS and DICES case study already appears in v2 A.11; JudgeBench is not an entirely new addition.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in corresponding experiments. The added ordinal Topical Chat analysis uses the Llama-3-70B evaluator already present in the case study and metric families already evaluated elsewhere in v2.

E3.justification: The added ordinal Topical Chat evaluation specifies 60 items per criterion, three human annotations, scales of 1–3 or 1–5, and percentage-agreement partitions (A.12.2, Table 11). Existing experiments retain their prompting, decoding, sampling and evaluation settings.

E4.justification: v3 extends the appendix case study with diagnostics of low ordinal human–machine correlations, examining label imbalance, constant human medians and rating discrepancies through Figures 8–11. Existing random-labeler simulations, toy examples and SNLI error examples are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report 20 sampled machine labels per example and retain the same plots with error bars. The added case study introduces no new repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: New Table 11 reports aggregate human–machine Krippendorff’s alpha values of -0.02, -0.07, -0.20 and -0.28 for Engaging, Maintains Context, Naturalness and Overall, respectively. These are additional task results; numerical values in matched existing tables and plots remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The binning and probability definitions, binned-JSD expression in Equations 1–2, and percentage-agreement formula in Equation 3 are unchanged. The existing toy counterexample moves from A.12 to A.8 without changing its mathematical content.

C1.justification: Both versions claim that aggregate correlations can conceal human–machine differences depending on human-label uncertainty. The principal contributions remain uncertainty stratification, binned JSD and perception charts; the rewritten abstract preserves their scope.

C2.justification: A.12.2 adds interpretations connecting low ordinal correlations to label imbalance and distinguishing possible prompt improvements from revisions to human annotation guidelines. Figure 9 explicitly identifies constant human medians as making rank correlation inapplicable. Existing limitations of bin-level aggregation remain.

D1.justification: The v3 abstract newly states that the authors’ analysis and visualization tools are open-sourced and supplies a repository address. v2 already includes metric and simulation code; those listings and the existing prompts remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The bibliography and substantive novelty framing are unchanged. Bavaresco et al. (2024), now mentioned with JudgeBench in Section 3, was already cited and used in v2’s appendix case study.

P1.justification: v3 edits the abstract, research-question wording and setup/results prose, moves the existing toy example from A.12 to A.8, and changes author order and conference headers. The main section structure and narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: v3 adds the ordinal Topical Chat dataset-summary display, Table 11 and Figures 8–11. It relocates existing main-text figures and tables, moves the toy-example tables, and adds item identifiers A–C to Table 4. Existing plot content is retained.

improvement.justification: The added ordinal case study makes the diagnostic value of stratification and perception charts more concrete, while the tool-repository link improves reproducibility information. These are modest gains over the retained core evidence. Some new commentary is imprecise: A.12.2 says roughly 30% receive machine median 3 for Engaging, whereas Figure 8 shows a majority. This limits the new explanation’s precision but does not outweigh its useful additional evidence.
